- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment intensity.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.4) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes (sentiment spike > 0.8) — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak to avoid overreaction.
- Lagged price movements (forecast 3–5 days ahead) often overpredict — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per lag day if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- Mean reversion bias in 10–14 day horizon — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or sentiment has recently declined.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 3–5 days are trending up, reduce forecast slope to avoid “momentum trap” unless sentiment confirms continuation.
